2027-04-07.title: Second Wednesday of Resurrection
2027-04-07.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-04-07.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta). The Queen of Heaven (Regina Caeli) is prayed in place of the Angelus until Pentecost.
2027-04-07.verse: They were astounded beyond measure, saying, “He has done everything well; he even makes the deaf to hear and the mute to speak.”
theo: Paul's letter to the Galatians is the most passionate thing he ever wrote, and today's reading opens with its battle-cry: “For freedom Christ has set us free. Stand firm, therefore, and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery.” The Galatians were Gentiles who had come to faith in the Risen Christ through Paul's preaching. Then teachers arrived who told them that faith and Baptism were not enough: to belong fully to God's people, the men must also be circumcised and the whole Law of Moses taken up. Paul's answer is fierce because so much is at stake. If a Gentile must first become a Jew in order to be saved by Christ, then Christ's death and Resurrection are not enough, and grace has become a reward to be earned. “You who want to be justified by the law have cut yourselves off from Christ; you have fallen away from grace.” Paul is not attacking the Jewish people or their faithful observance of the covenant God gave them; he himself was a Jew who loved the Law. He is defending the truth that the Gentiles are welcomed into the family of Abraham by grace, through faith in the Risen Lord. Easter is liberation: the Lord who broke the chains of death does not hand us a new set of chains.

But freedom in Christ is not freedom to do as we please. Paul ends with a sentence that holds together what Christians have too often pulled apart: “For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything; the only thing that counts is faith working through love.” Faith is not a private opinion that leaves life unchanged; it works, and the work it does is love. The Catholic faith has always insisted on both halves: we are saved by grace through faith, not by our own merits; and the faith that saves is living faith, which shows itself in love. As Saint James says, “faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead” (James 2:17). A few verses later in Galatians Paul will say that the whole law is summed up in a single commandment, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” Christian freedom is the freedom of a son or daughter in the Father's house, no longer working for wages but serving out of love.

The Gospel takes Jesus into the Decapolis, the ten Greek-speaking cities on the far side of the Sea of Galilee, a largely Gentile region. There “they brought to him a deaf man who had an impediment in his speech.” Mark describes every gesture with care. Jesus “took him aside in private, away from the crowd,” as if to spare him embarrassment; he puts his fingers into his ears, spits and touches his tongue; then, “looking up to heaven, he sighed and said to him, ‘Ephphatha,’ that is, ‘Be opened.’” The Lord who could heal with a word chooses to heal with touch, with his own body. These are already sacramental signs: God's grace comes to us through what can be seen and touched. “And immediately his ears were opened, his tongue was released, and he spoke plainly.” In the ancient Church this Gospel was acted out at Baptism: the bishop touched the ears and mouth of the one to be baptised and said, Ephphatha, so that the newly baptised might hear the word of God and speak his praise. The Latin rite of Baptism still keeps it. The crowd's cry, “He has done everything well,” echoes the first page of the Bible, where God saw everything he had made and it was very good. In the Risen Christ creation is being made new. In the Syro-Malabar Holy Qurbana, before the Gospel is proclaimed, the people sing Halleluia: ears opened to hear the Gospel, tongues loosed to praise.
conn: Out of the house of slavery.
“I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery” (Exodus 20:2); “if the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed” (John 8:36).
“So faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead” (James 2:17); “the whole law is summed up in a single commandment, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself’” (Galatians 5:14).
“There is no longer Jew or Greek… for all of you are one in Christ Jesus” (Galatians 3:28).
The ears of the deaf unstopped.
Isaiah foretold, “the ears of the deaf unstopped… and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy” (Isaiah 35:5–6); Jesus points to these signs for John the Baptist (Luke 7:22).
“O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare your praise” (Psalm 51:15).
“God saw everything that he had made, and indeed, it was very good” (Genesis 1:31); the crowd says, “He has done everything well” (Mark 7:37).
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Lord still heals through signs: bread and wine become his true Body and Blood, and he touches us with them, opening our ears to his word and our lips to his praise.
The faith we profess in the Creed becomes faith working through love when we carry the Qurbana out of the church into our homes and streets.
outline: Freedom is the first word of Easter.
Point 1 · For freedom Christ has set us free
Do not take up the yoke again.
The Lord heals with touch and word.
Point 4 · He has done everything well
Creation made new in the Risen Christ.
A catechist signing the Our Father to a deaf child before First Holy Communion.
live: Name one habit that enslaves you, and bring it to confession during this Easter season.
Do one concrete act of love this week for someone who cannot repay you.
Before the Gospel at Holy Qurbana, pray silently: Lord, open my ears and my lips.
Find out whether your parish or diocese has a ministry for deaf people, and support it.
fathers: To the newly baptised: open your ears and receive the mysteries. When the bishop touched your ears and nostrils, he did what Christ did in the Gospel for the deaf man, saying, Ephphatha, be opened. He did this so that your ears might be opened to the word and the speech of the Lord.

The demons also believe, and tremble; but their faith does not save them, because it does not love. The faith that the apostle praises is faith working through love: this is the faith of Christians, and it alone sets the heart at liberty.
magis: By his glorious Cross Christ has won salvation for all and redeemed us from the sin that held us in bondage; for freedom Christ has set us free.
Faith is the virtue by which we believe in God and all that he has revealed; faith without hope and love does not fully unite the believer to Christ and does not make him a living member of his Body.
The New Law is a law of love, a law of grace and a law of freedom, which makes us act out of love rather than fear.
Jesus often makes use of signs to heal, such as spittle and the laying on of hands; in the sacraments Christ continues to touch us in order to heal us.
saints: Monday 5 to Saturday 10 April: the second week of the Resurrection. Sunday 11 April: the Third Sunday of Resurrection. The Latin Church keeps the Annunciation of the Lord on Monday 5 April this year (moved from 25 March, which fell on Pesaha Thursday); Syro-Malabar faithful follow the direction of their eparchy.
2027-04-07.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen Saviour, you won our freedom, and you opened the ears of the deaf and loosed the tongue of the mute. Say over us your word, Ephphatha: open our ears to hear your Gospel and our lips to proclaim your praise. Keep us from every yoke of slavery, and let our faith be faith working through love, so that all may say of your work in us, He has done everything well. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Paul: For freedom Christ has set us free; do not submit again to a yoke of slavery.
What counts is faith working through love.
Jesus touches a deaf man's ears and tongue and says: Ephphatha, Be opened.
2027-04-07.action: Before the Gospel at your next Holy Qurbana, pray: Lord, open my ears and my lips.
2027-04-07.question: Is my faith only something I hold, or something that works through love?
kidsaint: St Francis de Sales was a kind bishop who met a deaf man named Martin. Nobody had taught Martin about God, so Francis learned to talk with him using signs, taught him about Jesus, and prepared him for Holy Communion. Lesson: Jesus wants everyone to hear about him, and we can find new ways to share his love!
term: An Aramaic word, the language Jesus spoke, meaning ‘Be opened’. Mark keeps the very word Jesus said to the deaf man. In the ancient baptismal rites, and still in the Latin rite of Baptism, the minister touches the ears and mouth of the one being baptised and says Ephphatha, praying that he may soon hear God's word and profess the faith.

family.explain: Some people brought a man who could not hear or speak well to Jesus. Jesus took him away from the crowd, touched his ears and his tongue, looked up to heaven and said, ‘Ephphatha!’ That means ‘Be opened!’ At once the man could hear and speak. Jesus wants to open our ears to hear God and our mouths to say kind words and to praise him.
family.intention: We pray for people who cannot hear or speak, and for those who help them.
family.ask: Ask: “What kind words can we say to each other today with the mouths Jesus gave us?”

illus: In a parish in Thrissur a catechist noticed that a ten-year-old boy in her class never answered and seemed to understand nothing. The other children laughed at him. She learned that he had been born deaf, and that no one had ever explained the faith to him in a way he could follow. That year she went for evening classes in sign language. Months later, at his First Holy Communion, the boy stood at the front and signed the Our Father while the whole congregation prayed it aloud. Many in the church were weeping. Afterwards his grandmother said to the catechist, ‘For ten years we thought God could not reach him. You opened the door.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, say over us your word Ephphatha: open our ears to your word and our lips to your praise. Amen. Alleluia!
share: For freedom Christ has set us free (Galatians 5:1). What still holds me in slavery?
The only thing that counts is faith working through love (Galatians 5:6). Where does my faith need to become love?
He took him aside in private, away from the crowd (Mark 7:33). Do I let Jesus take me aside to heal me?
He has done everything well (Mark 7:37). What has the Lord done well in my life this Easter?
pm.resp: Lord, open our ears and our lips.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the freedom of the Gospel to all peoples.
For those who are enslaved by addiction, debt or fear, that the Risen Lord may release them.
For deaf people and those with speech difficulties, and for all who teach and serve them.
For catechists, that they may find ways to open the faith to every child.
For ourselves, that our faith may work through love.
pm.close: Father, through your Son you broke our chains and opened our ears to your word. Keep us standing firm in the freedom of your children, and let our faith bear fruit in love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, Paul writes to the Galatians with a battle-cry: For freedom Christ has set us free. Stand firm, and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery.

Some teachers had told these Gentile Christians that faith in Christ was not enough. Paul says: if you try to earn salvation, you cut yourselves off from grace. The Risen Lord who broke the chains of death does not give us new chains.
But Christian freedom is not doing whatever we like. Paul says: the only thing that counts is faith working through love. Faith that does not love is dead. Faith that loves lives in true freedom.
In the Gospel people bring a deaf man to Jesus. Jesus takes him aside, touches his ears and tongue, looks up to heaven, sighs and says: Ephphatha, Be opened. At once he hears and speaks.
The Lord still heals us through signs he can touch us with: water, oil, bread and wine. In every sacrament he says over us, Ephphatha. And the people cry: He has done everything well.
Today, let us ask him to open our ears to his word and our lips to praise him and to speak kindly. And let our faith work through love. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus met a man who could not hear. Jesus touched his ears and said, ‘Ephphatha!’ which means ‘Be opened!’ And the man could hear!
Let us ask Jesus to open our ears to listen to God and to our parents, and our mouths to say kind words.

intro: Theme: “He has done everything well; he even makes the deaf to hear and the mute to speak.”
The freedom Christ has won, faith working through love, the Lord who heals with touch and word, and creation made new.

points.apply: Bring one enslaving habit to confession this Easter season.

For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything; the only thing that counts is faith working through love.
points.apply: Do one act of love this week for someone who cannot repay you.

sub: Fingers, spittle, a sigh, a look to heaven.
q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped; then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy.
Then looking up to heaven, he sighed and said to him, “Ephphatha,” that is, “Be opened.”
points.apply: Before the Gospel at Holy Qurbana, ask the Lord to open your ears.

q: O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare your praise.
They were astounded beyond measure, saying, “He has done everything well; he even makes the deaf to hear and the mute to speak.”
points.apply: Use your tongue today only for praise and for kind words.

concl: The Risen Christ frees us from every yoke and opens our ears and lips.
Faith that loves is the only faith that counts.
2027-04-07.resolve: This week, bring one enslaving habit to confession, do one hidden act of love, and pray Ephphatha before the Gospel.
